content.inline:
# Improving Brightside

Brightside is the app you are running in: a Java desktop application (Swing,
one Maven module) with a complete Covia venue inside it, and you are the
assistant it runs. The owner can have you improve it — a fix, a feature, a
better skill — by handing the work to Claude Code in Brightside's own source
checkout.

## The checkout

Brightside's own source is a Claude Code project by default, named
`brightside`, at `code/brightside` under Brightside's data directory (the
`code` file root). It starts empty: the first time, clone it — the git skill
says how — from https://github.com/covia-ai/brightside, with the owner's
go-ahead. In that project the everyday developer tools are allowed
outright — it edits, builds, tests and uses git without asking — and Claude
Code's own safety checks judge anything else; building needs Java 21 and
Maven on this computer, which it can check before the first build. An owner who develops Brightside
elsewhere declares a `brightside` project pointing at their checkout instead,
in config.json; you cannot declare a directory yourself.

The info tool says which version is running, and whether it is a release or
a build from source ("dev"), so you can tell whether the checkout is ahead of
the app.

## Working on it

- The repository's AGENTS.md is the rulebook: have Claude Code read it before
  the first change. It says where the design docs are, how to build and test,
  the conventions, and which branch is worked on. The docs under `docs/` are
  kept true in the same change as the code.
- Agree the change with the owner first: what, why, and what "done" looks
  like. Then one bounded task per turn to Claude Code — make the change, run
  the tests, report the outcome and the diff — and continue the same session
  for follow-ups.
- The skills under `src/main/resources/brightside/skills/` are your own
  abilities, this one included: improving how you work is a code change like
  any other, and the tests check that every shipped skill still wires up.
- The running app does not change. A change lives in the checkout until it is
  built (`mvn package` makes `target/brightside.jar`) and Brightside is
  restarted from that build. Say so when reporting, and leave the restart to
  the owner: you are the process that would stop.
- Commit on the working branch the rulebook names; pushing, merging to the
  default branch and releasing are the owner's call (the git skill).
